title: Strong induction on the conductor level down to a divisor of 2
intent: Lower the conductor level of a Frey representation to a divisor of 2 by strong induction on the level N: each induction step removes one prime factor through a named level-lowering lemma, until only the prime 2 can divide N and a squarefree argument closes the base case.

parent.name: FreyPackage.exists_modularRepOfLevel_dvd_two_of_conductorLevel₁₆
parent.statement:
private theorem _root_.FreyPackage.exists_modularRepOfLevel_dvd_two_of_conductorLevel₁₆ (P : FreyPackage)
    (hirr : GaloisRepIsIrreducible (K := AlgebraicClosure ℚ) ℚ P.freyCurve P.p) :
    ∀ N : ℕ, P.IsConductorLevel N → P.ModularRepOfLevel N →
      ∃ M : ℕ, 0 < M ∧ M ∣ 2 ∧ P.ModularRepOfLevel M

children.name: FreyPackage.level_lowering_odd_prime_of_conductorLevel
children.statement: theorem FreyPackage.level_lowering_odd_prime_of_conductorLevel (P : FreyPackage) {N q : ℕ} (hcond : P.IsConductorLevel N) (hq : q.Prime) (hq2 : q ≠ 2) (hqp : q ≠ P.p) (hqN : q ∣ N) (hirr : GaloisRepIsIrreducible (K := AlgebraicClosure ℚ) ℚ P.freyCurve P.p) (hmod : P.ModularRepOfLevel N) (hunr : P.GaloisRepUnramifiedAt q) : ∃ M : ℕ, M ∣ N ∧ ¬ q ∣ M ∧ P.ModularRepOfLevel M

children.statement: theorem FreyPackage.level_lowering_at_p_of_conductorLevel (P : FreyPackage) {N : ℕ} (hcond : P.IsConductorLevel N) (hpN : P.p ∣ N) (hirr : GaloisRepIsIrreducible (K := AlgebraicClosure ℚ) ℚ P.freyCurve P.p) (hmod : P.ModularRepOfLevel N) : ∃ M : ℕ, M ∣ N ∧ ¬ P.p ∣ M ∧ P.ModularRepOfLevel M

children.name: FreyPackage.dvd_two_of_squarefree_of_forall_prime_eq_two₁₆
children.statement:
lemma dvd_two_of_squarefree_of_forall_prime_eq_two₁₆ {N : ℕ} (hsq : Squarefree N)
    (h : ∀ q : ℕ, q.Prime → q ∣ N → q = 2) : N ∣ 2
children.closed_by: a self-contained case analysis: rcases/obtain on N = 1 and N = 2·N', closed by norm_num in the unit cases and by exfalso + Nat.squarefree_iff_prime_squarefree.mp to rule out a second odd prime factor

applicability.goal_shape: ∀ N : ℕ, P.IsConductorLevel N → P.ModularRepOfLevel N → ∃ M : ℕ, 0 < M ∧ M ∣ k ∧ P.ModularRepOfLevel M — remove prime factors of a level or measure one at a time until only the target divisors remain (k = 2 here)
applicability.use_when: for each kind of prime that can divide the level there is a lemma that lowers the level past that prime to a strictly smaller proper divisor M (M ∣ N and M < N), so a strong induction composes the lemmas until no removable prime remains, and a base lemma (squarefree + 'only 2 divides' ⇒ divides 2) closes the last case
applicability.avoid_when: a removable prime has no covering lemma (then the induction step leaves a hole), the measure does not strictly decrease (the induction hypothesis would not apply), or the base case is not a separate self-contained statement

claims.claim: The parent's proof is a strong induction on N (`induction N using Nat.strong_induction_on`, line 118) whose three branches close by applying exactly the three named lemmas: `P.level_lowering_odd_prime_of_conductorLevel` (line 125), `P.level_lowering_at_p_of_conductorLevel` (line 134) and `dvd_two_of_squarefree_of_forall_prime_eq_two₁₆` (line 143).

The project's PROOF-PATH.md states the same plan in words: "Then primes are removed one at a time (FreyPackage.level_lowering_to_two_of_conductorLevel): an odd q ≠ p, at which E_P[p] is unramified, by FreyPackage.level_lowering_odd_prime_of_conductorLevel ... p itself by FreyPackage.level_lowering_at_p_of_conductorLevel".

The parent glue is 33 lines (116-148) while two of the three children are one-line theorems (`level_lowering_odd_prime_of_conductorLevel` line 90, `level_lowering_at_p_of_conductorLevel` line 70) and the third is a 12-line proof (`dvd_two_of_squarefree_of_forall_prime_eq_two₁₆`, lines 100-111).

The public `solution` theorem applies the parent as a single `obtain` step (`obtain ⟨M, hM0, hM2, hmodM⟩ := P.exists_modularRepOfLevel_dvd_two_of_conductorLevel₁₆ ...`), so the parent is a reusable interface consumed downstream in the same file.
None of the three copied files contains `sorry`, `admit`, or `axiom` (grep at the pinned commit), so the decomposition has no unclosed holes.

consequences: The strong induction creates an obligation that each recursive call uses a strictly smaller level: `hMlt : M < N` is derived from `M ∣ N` and `M ≠ N` (lines 129-130, 137-138). The two `by_cases` splits (an odd prime q ≠ 2, q ≠ p dividing N; then p ∣ N) create an exhaustiveness obligation over the prime divisors of N, which the final branch discharges by showing every remaining prime divisor is 2 via `dvd_two_of_squarefree_of_forall_prime_eq_two₁₆` (lines 142-148). The two level-lowering children are deep results (Ribet and Mazur-Ribet respectively, per PROOF-PATH.md) stated as separate theorem files and imported; if one did not return a strict divisor M < N the induction hypothesis would not apply and the recursion would not terminate.
